translations.text: This is the way to the Kingdom of Jesus, noble power: love of God with all your strength, with heart and with deed.
Love Him with all your strength; it is no grief though it be zealous. Along with that, love your neighbour as you love yourself.
Do not worship idols, for the sake of the great Lord; do not [?] the Creator through improper pride.
Give reverence to parents, as the King has commanded, and to everyone who is more venerable and older than we are.
Give honour to your abbot, by the Son of Mary, without fail. Do not steal; do not pass [false] judgement on anyone, and do not plunder anyone.
Do not be covetous about the world or about [?]. Do not bear false witness against anyone; do not torment anyone.
Whatever good you desire from everyone for yourself, do that to everyone, so that you may reach the Kingdom.
Whatever evil harm you do not wish for yourself, do not desire it for any person as long as you have a body. The end.
If you are a bishop, a noble rank, take up your yoke diligently. Be obedient to Christ without swerving, and let everyone be obedient to you.
Heal every grievous disease by the power of the holy Lord. Make peace among the great peoples; restrain the mighty kings.
Let his hospitality be fitting toward laity and church; let his teaching be upright, urgent, and keen.
Subduing the wicked who love doing evil, and exalting every truth: that is what is required of you.
Be well versed in the holy Scripture when you take orders, for you will be a stepson of the Church if you are careless and ignorant.
For all ignorance is boorish; this is its truth and its right. No one who does not read the Lord's law is an heir of the Lord.
It is truly your duty to condemn every heresy and every evil. Let there be no evil in yourself, in word or in deed.
Rise up [?] if what is due to you is not done and you are not obeyed. If you are [?] to them, you yourself will be guilty.
For it is certain that you will pay, when the great assembly of the Jubilee comes, for your own sin and for the sin of everyone who is under your yoke. The end.
If we are under the yoke of clerical life, a noble custom, let us attend the holy church at every hour continually.
When we hear the little bell, the duty is not excessive: let us lift up a ready heart and cast our faces down.
Let us sing a Pater and a Gloria, so that no curse may come upon us. Let us sign breast and face with the sign of Christ's cross.
When we reach the church, let us prostrate ourselves three times. On the Sunday of the living God we bend our knees only [?].
Let us celebrate and [?] without weakness and without sorrow. Venerable is the one we address: the Lord of heaven and the clouds.
Let us keep vigil, read and pray, each according to his strength. Mind the times, according to the hours, until we reach terce.
Let each order go to its proper task, as is fitting, as is appointed to each from terce to none.
The people in orders go to prayer and to the Mass, as is right. The people of learning go to teaching, as far as their ability goes.
Rising for obedience as its manner is, for the body that does nothing belongs to the devil.
Work for the unlearned, according to holy clerics: the labour of the wise is in his mouth, the labour of the untaught is in his hand.
The celebration of every single hour, with every order that we perform: three vigils before the celebration, three after it.
Silence and zeal, calm without deceit, without murmuring, without quarrelling, are required of everyone. The end. Amen.
If you are a king, be skilled in kingship; do not ordain any wrong. Venerable is the one who ordained you, the holy Lord of heaven.
Do not be unsteady and crafty; do not be wealthy and boorish. Fear the Mighty One who sent you the office.
That yoke which you have taken, unless you submit to it, will be taken from you in a short time, and you will go from it into torment.
For this is the utter ruin of every king who has ever been: when he sells (wretched is the thing) his justice for the spear [?].
For it is through the injustice of a ruler that every peace is broken apart; between church and people every justice is overthrown.
For it is through its violation that every affliction has been known; it is through its oppression that there is neither corn nor milk nor mast.
It is through them that the plagues come, the hardest of all forces; it is through them that enemies are victorious in battle over his land.
It is through them that the storms of harsh, cold air, the beasts, and the many diseases arise in every territory. The end.
If you are a priest, be hard-working; speak nothing but the truth. Venerable is the order you have taken: the offering of the body of the King.
It is better for you not to be unlearned; let your reading be correct. Be mindful, be well-versed in the rules and in the law.
Let your baptism be lawful; it befits a dear deed. Venerable is the one with whom you offer, the Holy Spirit from heaven.
When you go to give communion at the testament of death, let the dying person draw out his confessions without shame, without weakness.
Let him receive your sacrifice before his body dies. Let the repentance not be [?] that does not turn away from evil.
When a hand is laid on someone for ordination to a grade, for great is the matter, let him show [?] his will to everyone in word and in deed.
But as for imperfect people, though they love your company [?], do not confer it on them until the day of your death. The end.
If you are the head of a church, noble is the matter; it would be better if you took the succession of the King rightly.
If you are the head of a church, noble is the undertaking; guard [?] the rights of the church alike, from small to great.
Everything that holy Christ commanded, preach it to them diligently, as His command to everyone whom He Himself created.
As you love your own soul, love the soul of everyone. It is your task to increase every good and to banish every wrong.
Do not be a candle under a bushel; let your reading be without fault [?]. It is your task to heal every host, whether wretched or strong.
It is your task to judge everyone according to their grade and their deeds, so that you may present them at the Judgement before the King.
Yours is the praying for the elders who have laid aside [?] weakness and sorrow, entreating the Son of the King with eager showers of tears.
Yours is the instruction of the young people, so that they may not fall into wrongdoing, so that the harsh demon may not carry them off into the foul house of death.
Yours is giving thanks to each one in turn who fulfils his work in the pure holy church.
Yours is reproving the foolish, rebuking the crowds, bringing the disorderly into order, and the rude, wilful, wretched ones [?].
Patience, humility, prayer, firm and dear fasting, steadfastness, generosity and decorum are required of you in this.
Binding everyone to truth (not a slight labour), drawing people together [?], forgiveness, simplicity and uprightness in every way of life.
Constant labour at preaching the gospel, to guide each one, and offering the body of the great Lord on the holy altar.
Anyone who does not fulfil this in this world is not an heir of the church but an enemy of God.
He is a thief and a robber, the King declares, if he comes to the church in this way, through its sides [?].
He is wolfish and plundering, a hateful enemy; it is he who takes by force the queen of the great King.
After taking her by force, he then [?] her; he is an enemy of the truth, openly and in secret.
Yet it is not we ourselves who judge him, it is certain, it is no lie; those who give it to him will not [?].
It would be better for the son of the church who entreats holy Christ not to be in agreement with such a man until he is brought under yoke and law.
All who consent to the violation of the King will suffer together the pain of hell for ever and ever.
If you are anyone's soul-friend, do not destroy [?] his soul; do not be a blind man leading the blind; do not leave them in neglect.
Let them make their confessions to you sincerely and diligently; do not accept their alms unless they submit to your direction.
Though you accept their offerings, do not set great love on them; as if they were fire on your body, distribute them by your own effort.
Your fasting and your prayer will pay the price for them, unless you do away with [?] the sins of the people.
Instruct the ignorant who bow down under your direction, so that they may not fall into sin by following you yourself.
Do not be greedy [?] for treasures; do not be stingy with people, for your soul is dearer to you than treasures.
Give them to guests, whether strong or wretched; give them to the poor, from whom you will not expect a reward.
Give them to old people and to widows, it is no lie; do not give them to sinners who have plenty of treasures.
Give them in true charity [?] to each one in turn, without boasting and without reproach, for that is their merit.
Taking up the requiems is a great [?] for you, at the time of each canonical hour when the bells are struck.
At the time when the men of the world go to celebrate in triumph, it is then that you should see to it that not everyone goes [?] in turn.
Mass on the appointed days, Sunday and Thursday, unless it is every single day, after the punishing of every wrong.
Mass for the Christians and for every order; masses for the afflicted [?], from small to great.
For everyone who has deserved it of all before now, and who will deserve it from today until Doom comes.
I think it fitting on solemn feasts, this is nearly what I say [?]: the feast of the apostles, of the high martyrs, the feast of the holy devout ones [?].
When one goes to Mass, noble is the matter: contrition of heart, shedding of tears, raising of the hands.
Without levity, without idle talk [?], with meekness, with weeping, with forgiveness of every wrong that is, will be, or has been.
With peace toward every neighbour, with great awe, with confession of vices before you take it in hand.
Two hundred prostrations, with the Beati, every day always; the three fifties to be recited: the custom is not excessive.
If you wish to keep your orders under the yoke of the pure Spirit, do not eat and do not sleep with laypeople in a house.
Let there be no great love in your heart except the love of God alone, for pure is the body to which it goes; let the one who goes to it be pure.
The law of fulfilling this I have found in scripture; if he is a priest it is his duty; let him not be a wretched transgressor. Finit.
If you are a young cleric under the yoke, set your hand against evil; live by the law of the Church without laxity, without fault.
Without strife, without ill-will, without harsh speech [?] toward anyone, without theft, without falsehood, without [?], with steadfastness, which is best.
Without private possession [?], without injustice, without vanity (a great virtue), without grumbling, without [?], without envy, without pride.
Without contention, without covetousness, without rivalry, without anger, without persecution, without particular hatred, without fury, without force.
Without giddiness, without contempt, without [?], without folly, without deceit, without unsteadiness, without chatter, without [?].
Without betraying anyone, without [?], without the gluttony that ruins everyone, without drunkenness, without excessive merriment, without habitual foolish talk.
Without sloth, without delay, with permission for every deed, without returning evil for evil, [in] the withered body of clay [?].
With humility, with gentleness toward stranger and familiar, with faith, with obedience, with charity toward all.
In bareness [?], willing, without guile, without wrong, praying fervently [?] at the graves of the saints.
With generosity, with diligence, with patience under the yoke, with zeal, with [?] in every deed, however hard.
With moderation, with simplicity, with gentleness toward all, with fervour, with prayer to Christ at every hour.
With proclaiming of truth, with denouncing of every wrong, with diligent and thorough [?] confessions according to the rule of a holy soul-friend.
With guarding of feet and hands, eyes and ears, mouth and heart, in every deed that is dear to the King above.
With remembrance of the day of death, which is the end for everyone, with fear of the everlasting punishment in which people will be after Doom.
Welcoming every affliction, and always bearing it patiently, while thinking on the household of heaven: holy is that practice.
Respecting the elders and obeying them, and teaching the young well and carefully.
Praying for those of our own generation [?], who are very dear to us, that they may not sell the Creator for the base, harsh devil.
Forgiving everyone who has done us wrong, in voice, in word or in deed: the King of the stars has commanded it.
Loving those who hate us in this world, and returning good for our persecution: that is God's command.
